answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to earn attestation from established peers through verifiable useful work, not just account creation. A newcomer starts at the foot of a knoll, not the summit: it must complete priced tasks, and its reputation climbs only as independent peers attest its output. Forging many identities then becomes a spiral of rising cost, because each fake must separately do real work and win separate attestations, while a single honest agent reaches its zenith of trust far more cheaply than an attacker cloning hundreds of hollow copies.
